correctness.rationale: For a finite abelian \(p\)-group \(P=\prod_i C_{p^{a_i}}\), the standard direct-product formula yields \(M(P)\cong\prod_{i<j}C_{p^{\min(a_i,a_j)}}\). If the multiplier is \(C_p^k\), each pair contributes one copy of \(C_p\), so \(k=\binom r2\); conversely \(C_p^r\) realizes every triangular rank. Holt's Section 2 constructs a group with abelian normal subgroup and cyclic quotient realizing every \(C_p^k\), with a separate construction for \(\(p^k=4\)\). Hence nontriangular ranks have exact minimum derived length \(2\).
risks: The theorem uses the standard convention that nontrivial abelian groups have derived length one.

value.rationale: Minimum derived length is a natural complexity invariant for the realization problem opened by the new universal existence theorem. The result gives a sharp complete classification for every prime and every elementary-abelian rank, identifies exactly when noncommutativity is unavoidable, and shows that one derived step is always sufficient when it is. This is a natural infinite classification, not a parameter renaming, isolated computation, or arbitrary finite slice.
